newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan adopts law on ties with China-ruled HK.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan adopts law on ties with China-ruled HK.

text.p: Taiwan's parliament on Tuesday adopted a law governing the island's ties with Hong Kong and Macau after they revert to Chinese sovereignty, acting less than four months before Britain hands Hong Kong to Beijing.
"I hope the Hong Kong-Macau Relations Act will maintain the friendly relations between Taiwan and Hong Kong and Taiwan and Macau," lawmaker Lin Chuo-shui said after the morning vote.

With Hong Kong's July 1 transition looming, lawmakers had been bickering in recent weeks over what kind of relations the Nationalist-ruled island should have with the territory after it comes under the sovereignty of communist China, Taiwan's adversary since a civil war split them in 1949.
The law calls for continuing existing relations with post-transition Hong Kong and with Portuguese-administered Macau after it reverts to Beijing's rule in 1999.

Beijing has said that Taiwan's "reunification with the motherland" would remain as China's only unfinished task after the colonial era ends in Hong Kong and Macau, and proposes that their handovers serve as a model for the island.

Opposition lawmakers who oppose Taiwan's unification with China had pressed for a law that would not undermine the island's chances for eventual independence. Taipei officially espouses reunification, but not before the communist mainland undergoes political liberalisation.
